entries.title: Psalms 35:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Say - By thy spirit assuring me of it: and by thy providence effecting it.

entries.title: Psalms 35:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Their way - By which they flee, being chased.

entries.title: Psalms 35:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: My bones - My whole body, as well as my soul.

entries.title: Psalms 35:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Returned - Although my fastings and prayers did them no good.

entries.title: Psalms 35:15
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Gathered - They were so full of joy, that they could not contain it in their own breasts, but sought to communicate it to others. Abjects - Or, vile persons, either for the meanness of their condition, or for their wickedness. Knew not - While I had no suspicion of them. Tear me - My good name with calumnies, and reproaches and curses.

entries.title: Psalms 35:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Mockers - They made themselves buffoons and jesters, and accustomed themselves to mock and deride David, that thereby they might gain admittance to the tables of great men, which was all they sought for.

entries.title: Psalms 35:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Look on - Without affording me pity or help. Darling - My soul, Heb. my only one; which is now left alone and forsaken by my friends, and hath none to trust in but God.

entries.title: Psalms 35:18
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: I will - When I shall be restored to the liberty of the publick assemblies.

entries.title: Psalms 35:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: For - They breathe out nothing but threatenings and war; they use not open violence but subtile artifices, against me and my followers, who desire nothing more than to live quietly and peaceably.

entries.title: Psalms 35:21
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Wide - To pour forth whole floods of scoffs and slanders. ha - An expression of joy and triumph. Our eye - What we have long desired and hoped for.

entries.title: Psalms 35:22
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: This - Thou also hast seen, all their plots and threats, and all my distresses and calamities. Keep not - Be not deaf, to my prayers. The same word signifies, both to be silent, and to be deaf.

entries.title: Psalms 35:23
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Awake - To plead my cause against mine adversaries.
